source.notes: Very large (11105 x 24176 px, 72 MB) scan of the whole hanging scroll including the silk mounting and the Qianlong-era title slip; PD-Art of a c. 1000 painting. The 800 px preview was checked and is clean. Dimensions 206.3 x 103.3 cm, dates (1000–1020) and NPM inventory 故畫000826 from Wikidata Q15907822 and zh.wikipedia '谿山行旅圖'. Fan Kuan's dates from en.wikipedia (c. 960 – c. 1030; Wikidata gives 956–1026, zh.wikipedia c. 950 – c. 1032). Place of painting is not recorded; madeIn uses the painter's native Huayuan (today Yaozhou District, Tongchuan, Shaanxi, per zh.wikipedia), coordinates from Wikidata Q1201033. No English Wikipedia article exists for the painting, so the painter's article is linked.

object.movement: Northern Song monumental landscape (Northern Landscape style)
object.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour on silk
object.description: A single cliff face rises almost the full height of the silk, with a thread of waterfall at its right and a mule train and travellers reduced to specks along the stream at its foot. Fan Kuan, a recluse who studied the mountains of Shaanxi directly, painted it around 1000; it is the defining work of Northern Song monumental landscape. The painter's signature, hidden among the foliage at lower right, was only rediscovered in 1958.
facts: Ink and light colour on silk, 206.3 by 103.3 cm, in the National Palace Museum, Taipei.
Fan Kuan's half-hidden signature in the leaves at the lower right was rediscovered in 1958.
The Ming painter-critic Dong Qichang is said to have called it the finest painting of the Song dynasty.
